items.note: Arjunavarman's Piplianagar grant describes the Paramāras of Dhārā beginning with Bhōjadēva, followed by Udayāditya who stripped off the glory of his adversaries; then Naravarman, Yaśōvarman, Ajayavarman, Vindhyavarman.
Editor takes nity-otsāhaika-kautukī of Udayāditya to mean 'whose sole delight was to perform deeds of valour'; he subdued the enemies who had overpowered the kingdom in Bhōjadēva's last days.
Poetic records name Yaśōvarman's son Ajayavarman, prose records Jayavarman; editor holds them identical, name changed to suit the metre (against Kielhorn).
Vindhyavarman liberated the Paramāra kingdom suffered at Chaulukya hands since Yaśovarman, whose kingdom Jayasinha Siddharāja had captured.
